summary: Magdalene Sophie Schott was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the universities of Tübingen, Münster, Berlin, Freiburg, and Marburg, completing her PhD at Heidelberg University (1928–1935) under Max Walleser.

Maggie Bickford is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at Bennington College, Yale, and Princeton. She held appointments at Brown University, including Professor of East Asian Studies around 1987, and was a member at IAS (1999–2000).

Mahadev Govind Ranade (1842–1901) was an Indian scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and Government Law College, Mumbai, and founded the Maharashtra Girls Education Society in 1885.

Mahakachchakodiye Pangngasekara specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2020–2023) and served as Senior Lecturer II at Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka (2020–2024).
Mahala Rethlake is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She pursued a PhD in Religious Studies (Philosophy of Religions) as a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago through 2026.
Mahananda Timilsina is an Indologist. He earned his PhD from Nepal Sanskrit University by 2015 and held an academic post there.

Maharshi Vyas is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He was a PhD student at the University of California (2017–2025) and became an assistant professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2025.

Mahasi Sayadaw (1904–1982) was a Buddhist studies and religious figure. He studied under U Narada, Aletawya Sayadaw, and Thelon Sayadaw, served as abbot at Taung-waing-galay Taik Kyaung, taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, and founded Insight Meditation Society in 1979.
Mahaveer H. Muhammad works in history, archaeology, linguistics, and Indology. He earned an M.A. from Shah Abdul Latif University and served as a researcher for the Government of Sindh.

Mahendradatta Jayadi is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA in Buddhist Studies at International Buddhist College (2010–2013) and a Diploma in Pali at Somaiya Vidyavihar University (2022–2023).

Mahendranath Gupta (1854–1932) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Hare School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, he held posts at Ripon College and Surendranath College around 1885.

Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1996–2002), where he became Head in 2006, and serves as a regional representative for the Pali Text Society.

Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University, attested in 1882, 1894, and 1914.
Mahesh Kumar is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA Hons at Banaras Hindu University (2015–2020) and became a research scholar there in 2021.
Mahinda Deegalle is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Peradeniya, Harvard, and Chicago, he held posts at Bath Spa University, Cambridge, and SOAS, among other institutions.
Mahiro Ito (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021. He has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University.

Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Otani University by 2008 and served as a visiting researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, attested in 2010.

Mai Mishiro is a scholar in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. Her career includes affiliations with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tsukuba and Toyo University, serving as Toyo's president from 2009 to 2020.

Makio Ueno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who received a PhD from Otani University in 2009. He has held positions at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute, Otani University, and Otani Academic Society.
